q: In a circular motion, the object just moves in a circle.
e: True. Circular motion means the object travels on a circular path. That is not yet a whole body spinning about an axis.

q: In a circular motion, the object rotates about an axis.
e: False. Circular motion is travel on a circular path. Rotation of a whole body about an axis is rotational motion.

q: An example of circular motion is artificial satellites going around the earth at a constant height.
e: True. An example of circular motion is artificial satellites going around the earth at a constant height. A satellite at constant height travels on a circle around Earth, which is circular motion.

q: In rotational motion, the object rotates about an axis.
e: True. In rotational motion, the object rotates about an axis. Rotational motion means a body spins about an axis.

q: Rotation of earth about its own axis which creates the cycle of day and night is an example of circular motion.
e: False. Earth spinning on its own axis is rotational motion, not circular motion of a point on a circle. The error is the part about Rotation earth own axis creates cycle.

q: Motion of the blades of a fan is an example of rotational motion.
e: True. Motion of the blades of a fan is an example of rotational motion. Fan blades spin as a whole about the motor axis, so that is rotational motion.

q: Motion of a Ferris wheel in an amusement park is an example of rotational motion.
e: True. Motion of a Ferris wheel in an amusement park is an example of rotational motion. A Ferris wheel turns about its central axle, so the wheel is in rotational motion.

q: A rigid body is a body that does not deform or change shape.
e: True. A rigid body is a body that does not deform or change shape. A rigid body does not deform, so its shape stays the same.

q: A rigid body is a body that deforms slightly when the distance between any two particles within the body changes.
e: False. If particle distances change, the body is not rigid. The error is the part about rigid body deforms slightly distance particles.

q: In a rigid body, no matter how the body moves, the distance between any two particles within the body remains constant.
e: True. In a rigid body, no matter how the body moves, the distance between any two particles within the body remains constant. Particle-to-particle distances stay fixed in a rigid body, whatever the motion.

q: If a rigid body is in rotational motion, all the particles constituting it undergo circular motion about a common axis.
e: True. If a rigid body is in rotational motion, all the particles constituting it undergo circular motion about a common axis. Every particle of a rigid rotor rides its own circle about the same axis.

q: If a rigid body is in rotational motion, only the particles on the surface undergo circular motion about a common axis.
e: False. Every particle of a rigid rotor moves in a circle about the common axis, not only the surface. The error is the part about rigid body rotational motion particles surface.

q: When an object rotates, it can speed up or slow down.
e: True. When an object rotates, it can speed up or slow down. A rigid rotor can raise or lower ω, and then it has angular acceleration.

q: During the time intervals when an object speeds up or slows down, its angular velocity is changing therefore it has an angular acceleration.
e: True. During the time intervals when an object speeds up or slows down, its angular velocity is changing therefore it has an angular acceleration. Changing ω, whether speeding up or slowing down, is angular acceleration α.

q: If an object's angular velocity changes at a constant rate, the angular acceleration is constant.
e: True. If an object's angular velocity changes at a constant rate, the angular acceleration is constant. If ω changes at a steady rate, α itself is a constant.

q: If an object's angular velocity changes at a constant rate, the motion is called the rotational motion under constant linear acceleration.
e: False. A constant rate of change of ω is constant angular acceleration, not linear acceleration. The error is the part about object angular velocity changes constant rate.

q: Rotational variables such as angular displacement, angular velocity, and angular acceleration are applied to analyze the rotational motion for a rigid body about a fixed axis under a constant angular acceleration.
e: True. Rotational variables such as angular displacement, angular velocity, and angular acceleration are applied to analyze the rotational motion for a rigid body about a fixed. θ, ω and α are the rotational variables used to analyse spinning motion.

q: The kinematic equations for rotational motion can be derived in terms of the angular displacement, angular velocity and angular acceleration of the object at any instant of time.
e: True. The kinematic equations for rotational motion can be derived in terms of the angular displacement, angular velocity and angular acceleration of the object at any instant. The constant-α kinematic equations are written in θ, ω and α.

q: The initial angular speed is the magnitude of angular velocity of the object at $t=0$.
e: True. The initial angular speed is the magnitude of angular velocity of the object at t=0. Initial angular speed is |ω| at the starting instant t = 0.

q: The initial angular speed is the magnitude of angular velocity of the object at $t=1$.
e: False. Initial angular speed is the magnitude of ω at t = 0. Initial means the starting instant t = 0, not t = 1.

q: The equations of motion for constant angular acceleration are the same as those for linear motion, with the angular quantities replaced with corresponding linear ones.
e: True. The equations of motion for constant angular acceleration are the same as those for linear motion, with the angular quantities replaced with corresponding linear ones. Angular acceleration α is the rate of change of angular velocity ω.

q: The equations of motion for constant angular acceleration are completely different from those for linear motion with constant acceleration.
e: False. The constant-α equations are analogues of the constant-a linear equations, not a different family. The error is the part about equations motion constant angular acceleration completely.

q: The equations for constant angular acceleration in rotational motion are analogous to equations for constant acceleration in linear motion.
e: True. The equations for constant angular acceleration in rotational motion are analogous to equations for constant acceleration in linear motion. The constant-α rotation equations match the constant-a linear set, with θ, ω, α in place of s, v, a.
